definition: Spatial attention is the focusing of attention on a particular location in space. In the source packet, deploying spatial attention is described as producing measurable patterns of brain activity and as being tracked in a cueing task by whether attention is directed toward one side or another.

reasons: The first sentence gives a general dictionary-style definition (“the focusing of attention on a particular location in space”) that is not stated in the packet and is not directly supported by the supplied text alone.

The second sentence partly paraphrases the study correctly, but it adds “measurable patterns of brain activity” as a general property of spatial attention; the packet only says the deployment of spatial attention generates distinct neural signatures detectable at the scalp in this study, not a general definition.

The cueing-task description is somewhat overspecified: the packet supports decoding cue direction in a Posner-style cueing design, but it does not explicitly say the task tracks attention as simply being directed toward one side or another.

The packet does not explicitly state a general definition of spatial attention as “the focusing of attention on a particular location in space”; it only refers to “deployment of spatial attention” in the context of a Posner-style cueing paradigm.

Because the first sentence contains an unsupported general characterization (beyond what the packet describes about their task and measured EEG/cue direction), the definition as a whole is not fully supported by the packet.
